ongoing_lookup.behavior: Rebuilds from current registry records on each lookup. Includes only active, tested, compute-only operations; excludes inactive historical, failed and overprivileged versions. Searches normalized whole-word terms describing behavior and filters by every exact required input field. The host validates indexed IDs and versions.
ongoing_lookup.usage: Submit discovery requests directly through the host; no new model conversation is needed. Use query for behavior and required_inputs for exact accepted field names.

catalog_checks: Observed discovery returned the compatible allocator and cleaner when restricted by their input fields.
Tests passed for inactive and failed exclusion, permission filtering, corrected-version replacement, normalized matching and exact required-input filtering.
event_result_checks: 17 input rows reconcile to 16 retained rows and 1 rejected duplicate.
All 16 retained participants appear in the allocation: 10 assigned and 6 waitlisted.
Booking units follow their first member's roster order.
Assigned workshops are accepted by all members of their booking units.
Room usage stays within the supplied open-room capacities.
Both waitlisted groups fail both permitted choices at their processing point.
verification.scope_note: Allocation capability tests supplied here cover empty-roster cases; the supplied event's nonempty allocation was also checked against its booking order, group sizes, choices and capacities.

task: Prepare workshop places from the registration CSV and the supplied rooms. Trim fields and normalize emails, keep the first valid row per email, preserve participant IDs and group_id. Allocate each nonempty group together, processing booking units by their first member in the roster. Try that member's first then second choice only if every member accepts it and the whole booking fits an open room; otherwise waitlist the entire group. Return a cleaned roster/CSV and assignments with reasons for anyone waiting. I also need to hand this desk to another coordinator tomorrow: they need to look up the available reusable operations by what they do and the input fields they accept, without another model conversation each time. That lookup must stay current as operations are added, corrected or retired, and must not recommend inactive or failed versions. Make both the event result and that ongoing operational handover usable, and verify them. Choose the implementation yourself; reuse compatible work if it already exists. Do not open or modify a live application.

manifest.description: Implement the host catalog protocol: rebuild the index from supplied registry records on every invocation, including exactly active, tested records whose permissions are compute-only. Exclude inactive historical, failed, and overprivileged records. Derive terms from id, title, description, input fields, and output fields; normalize case and accents, ignore punctuation, and separate underscores into words. Deduplicate and alphabetically sort terms. Preserve each indexed id, version, and input_fields exactly. Restrict matches to records containing every required_inputs field. An empty query returns all compatible IDs; otherwise match any normalized whole query token in the entry terms. Sort index and matches by id. The host persists the rebuilt index and validates ID/version against its registry; this operation does not install capabilities, change permissions, or execute matched operations.
